To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the screw dislocations forming a (001) twist boundary in silicon are dissociated, and that the dissociation is associated with the formation of extended point defect structures at the dislocation intersections.

the screw dislocation intersections are characterized by closed characteristic point defects (extended point defects) which are different in the case of a twist or a tilt boundary, and that the dislocation intersections have the same atomic structure as the dislocation cores in a perfect crystal.

(a/2)[110] screw dislocation intersections in Si generate extended point defects (EPDs), which are characteristic of the dislocation configuration and the boundary plane, and the EPD structures depend on the number of dislocations in the arrays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the atomic structure and properties of dislocation intersections in silicon.
the atomic structures of dislocation intersections in silicon.
the atomic structure of extended defects formed in the cores of dislocation intersections, and with the role of these defects in the generation of the low-angle twist and shear boundaries in silicon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dislocation cores at intersections of screw dislocations in Si have the same structure as the cores of the individual dislocations, and the core of a dislocation intersection is a closed characteristic group of atoms.
screw dislocations forming a regular two-dimensional network in silicon are characterized by a large variety of extended point defect structures at their intersections.
the dislocation intersections in silicon are not formed by a single point defect, but are composed of a number of point defects, which are not identical to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atomic configurations of extended defects at the dislocation intersections have a pronounced effect on the dislocation core energy and, consequently, the dislocation mobility.

the dislocation intersections in the twist boundary are formed by a single extended point defect with a D4h symmetry (the D4h defect), and that in the shear boundary they are formed by two extended defects with D4d symmetry (the D2d defect and the D4 defect).

the atomic structure of the dislocation core at the intersection is not a simple superposition of the core structures of the individual dislocations but rather depends on the dislocation configuration as a whole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extended point defects at the screw dislocation intersections are not necessarily associated with the dissociation of dislocations, but can be formed even in undissociated dislocations.
the extended point defect configurations at dislocation intersections can be used for identification of the screw dislocation type and for characterization of the dislocation arrays in silicon.
the dislocation intersections may act as effective sinks for vacancies and self-interstitials.
